architecture.mechanism: Multi-bearing multi-objective collaborative optimization of the lubrication system to reduce over-lubrication by matching circulating flow rate to operating speed, improving oil film thickness and lowering oil consumption.
architecture.intervention: Reconfigure the engine's oiling circuit to a multi-bearing, speed-dependent delivery scheme that reduces circulating flow rate (~6%) and eliminates over-lubrication, implemented via calibrated bearing/main-gallery restrictors and a revised oil-pump flow curve tied to rpm; retain factory 5w-30 conventional oil and preserve all sealed OEM interfaces so no external leaks are introduced and the repair remains warranty-compliant.
architecture.expected_effect: Lower oil consumption (returning oil-life/low-oil-light behavior to normal service intervals) without external leakage and without deviating from the dealer-specified 5w-30 conventional fill, by suppressing the over-lubrication-driven oil burn while keeping the lubrication regime within OEM envelope.
architecture.falsification_test: On the same vehicle, perform three back-to-back 1,000-mile consumption tests (engine run on dynamometer or controlled road loop) at 800, 1800, and 2800 rpm-equivalent duty cycles, measuring oil used per 1,000 mi; compare pre- and post-modification results, and inspect the entire external oil circuit (valve cover, oil pan, front/rear seals, oil filter housing, PCV system) for any wetness or drips to confirm no new external leak path was introduced.
